messages.content: is my sister study after dinner right?
use my sister studies after dinner. studies goes with my sister in that sentence.
now make it about me.
i study after dinner.
now say she did it yesterday.
my sister studied after dinner yesterday.
what if she is doing it now?
my sister is studying now.
can you use studies and studied in one sentence?
my sister studies after dinner, and she studied after dinner yesterday too.
only give the sentence about yesterday.
my sister studied after dinner yesterday.
now only give the longer example with both again.
my sister studies after dinner, and she studied after dinner yesterday too.
write a longer story about a family making a meal. use cooks, washes, and carries. the small problem should be when each part is ready.

a father cooks while his daughter washes cups at the kitchen table. his son carries bread into the next room. the daughter asks whether she should carry the cups too, but the father says he still needs one for water while cooking. she leaves one with him and takes the rest to the meal table. the son comes back for the soup before it is ready. instead of making him wait with a full container in his hands, the father asks him to make a place for it first. each person has a part to do, but the order is important too. when the soup is ready, the son carries it, the daughter brings the last cup, and the father sits down with them. the meal works because they ask what is ready, not just what each person has been told to carry.
what does the daughter wash?
she washes cups.
what does the son carry first?
he carries bread into the next room.
why does one cup stay with the father?
he needs it for water while cooking.
only tell me the useful order for the food and cups.
the bread goes first. the soup goes when ready, and the last cup comes after the father is done with it.
finish with a simple line at the table.
they pass the bread and begin eating together.
change i carry the book to my brother.
my brother carries the book.
now use he instead.
he carries the book.
why not he carry?
with he in that sentence, use carries. with i or they, use carry.
now make it yesterday.
he carried the book yesterday.
ask if he did it yesterday.
did he carry the book yesterday?
why carry after did?
did goes with carry in that question. carried works without did in he carried the book yesterday.
only give the brother sentence again.
my brother carries the book.
hey. somebody remembered a book i said i wanted to read and asked me about it today.
hi. what was it like to hear that they remembered?
it felt nice. i had said it only once.
a small detail can feel important when somebody keeps it in mind and asks again.
can you help me write a thank you without making it sound like they bought the book?
thank you for asking about the book i wanted to read. it was nice that you kept it in mind.
only give the thank you for asking.
thank you for asking about the book i wanted to read.
can i just say that last part?
it was nice that you kept it in mind.
does that say i have read it already?
no. it says somebody asked about it, not that you finished reading it.
only give the thank you again.
thank you for asking about the book i wanted to read.
is my father washes the cup a full sentence?
yes. it can say what he usually does, or be part of a story about what happens.
make that explanation shorter.
yes. it says what he does.
now make it yesterday.
my father washed the cup yesterday.
now tell him to do it in a kind way.
could you wash the cup, please?
why not washes in that question?
could you goes with wash, not washes. washes works with my father or he in the sentence you first gave.
now use they as the people doing it.
they wash the cup.
only give the first sentence again.
my father washes the cup.
write a longer story about a woman who fixes a chair for a neighbor. the neighbor likes its old color, so she asks before changing more than the broken part.

a woman fixes things in a small room behind her house. one day, a neighbor brings a chair with a broken part. the woman looks at it and asks what the neighbor wants kept the same. the neighbor says the brown color is important because the chair came from their father. the woman says she can work on the broken part without changing the whole chair. when the neighbor comes back, the chair can be used again and still looks like the one they remember. the neighbor thanks her for asking before making it new in every way. fixing a problem had not needed to mean changing every detail from the past. the woman puts the tool away and asks whether the chair feels ready for the place it will be used.
what does the woman fix?
she fixes a broken part of the chair.
what does the neighbor want kept?
the old brown color and the way the chair is remembered.
make the important idea of the story more simple.
the woman changes the broken part without changing every other thing about the chair.
why ask before changing the color?
she needs to ask why the neighbor wants to keep it.
make that answer shorter.
the color may have a meaning she does not know yet.
finish with the chair back at home.
the neighbor puts the chair by the table and sits in it to read, seeing the same brown color as before.
give me a sentence with sleeps about a baby in a story.
the baby sleeps in the next room.
now use slept and yesterday.
the baby slept in the next room yesterday.
what if it is happening now?
the baby is sleeping in the next room now.
can you know how long from those sentences?
no. they say where and when, not how many hours.
make that answer shorter.
no number of hours was given.
now ask whether the baby slept.
did the baby sleep in the next room?
only give the first sleeps sentence again.
the baby sleeps in the next room.
there are three garments on a chair and two in a container. how many garments is that if they are all different objects?
five garments.
can you know what kind each one is?
no. garment is a general word. you have not given the specific kind of any of them.
now i say one is a pink dress. is that still a garment?
yes. it can be one of the five garments in your group.
make that answer shorter.
yes. a dress can be a garment.
if i take the dress out, how many garments are left?
four garments.
can you know all the other garments are pink too?
no. you gave the color of the dress, not every garment.
only give how many were there at the start.
five garments.
i want to buy a book, but i do not know the price. give me a short question for the shop.
how much does this book cost?
can i ask if i can pay tomorrow without saying they already told me yes?
could i pay tomorrow, or do i need to pay now?
only explain whether that question gives a sure yes.
the question asks whether tomorrow is okay. it does not say they already said yes.
what if they say i need to pay now?
then you can choose whether to buy it now or leave it. the question gave them a way to tell you the rule.
can you know i have enough money?
no. you have not given the price or how much money you have.
only give the first question again.
how much does this book cost?
use listens in a sentence about my sister and a story.
my sister listens to the story.
now make it yesterday.
my sister listened to the story yesterday.
can i say she listens without to the story?
yes. she listens can be a full sentence if context makes clear what she listens to.
now ask her to do it.
please listen to the story.
why listen and not listens in that request?
when asking someone to do it this way, use listen. listens goes with she in the sentence about what she does.
can you know she understood every word?
no. listening and understanding every word are different facts.
only give the sister sentence again.
my sister listens to the story.
write a longer story about a person giving someone a book to read, but not yet making it theirs to keep. let a question keep the meaning clear.

a man gives his wife a book while she is sitting near the window. she asks whether he wants her to read one part or keep the whole book. he says that he wants to show her a story he found, and that the book came from the library. she thanks him and reads the first page. later, she puts it back with his things so he can return it. the small question had made clear that give in the moment was about putting it in her hands, not making it her own. another day, he buys her a book of her own and says that this one is hers to keep. giving a book looked similar on each day, but the words around it gave a different meaning.
why did she ask whether she should keep it?
she wanted to know whether the book was being given as her own or only for reading a part.
where had the first book come from?
the library.
make the difference between the two books more simple.
the first book was for her to read a part, then return. the other book was hers to keep.
what made the later book different?
he bought it for her and said she could keep it.
finish with the two books in different places.
she put her own book on her shelf and kept the library book with the things ready to go back.
that helped me ask the question better. do not add a new task.
you are welcome. we can leave it there.
can you just say a kind goodbye?
goodbye, and take care.
only one word now.
goodbye.
